claim.headline: For closed orientable surface groups of genus g>=2, L(pi_1 Sigma_g) = L(F_{2g-1}); more generally for every finitely generated torsion-free non-elementary discrete Gamma < PSL_2(R), L(Gamma) is a free group factor, settling the de la Harpe-Voiculescu conjecture in the torsion-free case.
claim.theorem_1_as_reported: Gamma(g; m_1..m_k : t, s): L(Gamma) = L(F_r), r = 2g-1+s+t+sum(1-1/m_j), if t+s>0, or g>=2, or (g>=1 and k>=2). [statement as relayed by WebFetch; verify]
claim.theorem_2: Any f.g. non-elementary discrete Gamma < PSL_2(R): L(Gamma) contains a free group factor as a finite-index subfactor and sits with finite index in an interpolated free group factor.
claim.theorem_3_main_technical: For every eta>0 there is a Haar unitary v in L(F_2) with ||v-A||_2<eta and L(F_2) = W*(w) * W*(v), where w = ABA^{-1}B^{-1}.
claim.theorem_4: Closed surfaces S with chi(S)<0 (including non-orientable): L(pi_1 S) = L(F_{1-chi(S)}).
claim.proposition_3: A product of commutators w = c_1...c_n in L(F_{2n}) is freely complemented, with complement L(F_{2n-1}).
claim.self_limitation: Section 1 says the author is unable to settle the de la Harpe-Voiculescu conjecture in all cases (torsion).

architecture: Prop 1 (Baire): if for all finite x_1..x_n and eps,eta>0 there is an automorphism theta with theta(w)=w, ||theta(A)-A||_2<eta and sum ||x_i - E_{theta(N)} x_i||_2^2 < eps (N = W*(A,w)), then for every delta there is a Haar v free from w with ||v-A||_2<delta and M = W*(w)*W*(v). Proof: Baire category in the L2-closure X of the orbit {theta(A): theta(w)=w}; generation from L2-totality.

Prop 2: replaces E_N by positive contractions T_k (T_0=E_N, T_k -> id) with forms Q_k; the hypothesis is a one-step improvement Q_k -> Q_{k+1}; proof telescopes with budgets eps/(2J), eta/(2J) chosen backward.

Section 3: T_q = radial multiplier q^{l(g)}, l = Bass-Serre length relative to H = <A,w>. Automorphisms S_f: A->Af(B), B->B; R_m: A->A, B->BA^m (Nielsen transvection fixing H); Psi_{f,m} = R_{-m} o S_f o R_m, so Psi(A) = A f(BA^{-m}) and Psi(w) = w. f_{m,t}(z) = exp(i sqrt(t/2m)(z+zbar)) gives ||f-1||_2 <= sqrt(t/m) per step. Lemma 9: Q_q(theta_{m,t}^{-1}(B)) >= F_t(q) - eps; iterating q_{j+1} = F_{t_j}(q_j) drives q_j up to 1. Lemma 10 verifies the hypothesis of Prop 2.
Section 4: amalgamated free products over W*(w), surface groups, non-orientable surfaces.

comparison.detail: Same architectural role: a small automorphism (L2-small on A, fixing w) that improves how well the perturbed subalgebra approximates prescribed targets (Lemma 10 = hypothesis of Prop 1/2). 287's version is norm-small, fixes nothing, and makes one extra free generator C approximable by a word, so the free rank drops. Shlyakhtenko keeps rank 2 and complements a fixed element. The mechanisms differ: explicit finite automorphisms with Fourier estimates, against a flow with a cocycle.
evidence: Lemma 1: "the map A->Af(B), B->B extends to a normal trace-preserving automorphism"
Lemma 5: Psi_{f,m}(A) = A f(BA^{-m}), Psi_{f,m}(w) = w

comparison.detail: No 1-cocycles, Fox derivatives, prefix sums 1+sum lambda(p_j), free Poisson/Marchenko-Pastur law, spectral-cutoff inverse, Haagerup inequality, or l2-cohomology. Closest analogue: the 1/sqrt(m)-per-step, O(1)-cumulative scaling of f_{m,t} along the long word BA^{-m} (Lemma 9's exponential limit). That is the same amplification principle in a different formalism.

comparison.item: S = Arg(C) bounded logarithm (I07; trace insight backtrack d1.2->d1.3)
comparison.detail: Unnecessary there: S_f is an exact automorphism defined by functional calculus of B. The only logarithm in the paper is scalar (Section 3.4). The nearest precedent for Arg(C) is Ioana-Peterson-Popa 2008 (Borel f with exp(i pi f(z)) = z), not this preprint.

comparison.item: adaptive error-budget iteration (I34) and L2 generation (I35)
comparison.detail: Both papers produce the new generator(s) as limits of images under compositions of small automorphisms and prove generation through L2-totality. Shlyakhtenko uses Baire category (Prop 1) plus backward telescoping budgets (Prop 2). 287 uses an explicit forward diagonal with future budgets fixed after each witness word, plus a conditional-expectation argument. 287 flags the parallel itself (main.tex:105).

comparison.item: Nielsen correction (gamma: C -> C A_w; alpha = gamma^{-1} o beta; I32)
comparison.detail: Both papers conjugate or compose a non-group 'small' automorphism with a Nielsen transvection that fixes the protected subgroup: R_m fixes H = <A,w>, while gamma fixes the A_j. The purposes differ. R_m moves the perturbation onto a long word to control cancellations; gamma retargets C A_w to C.
evidence: Lemma 2: "the map A->A, B->BA^m extends to a normal trace-preserving automorphism"

shlyakhtenko_check.bearing_on_free_group_factor_problem: None directly. The identifications have r = 1 - chi(Gamma), consistent with both branches of the Dykema-Radulescu dichotomy, and the free rank never changes (Prop 3: 1 + (2n-1) = 2n). Its relevance is methodological. It shows, two weeks before 287, that small automorphisms plus a limiting generation argument can produce new free generating sets in L(F_n). 287's new ingredient is the mechanism that makes the free rank drop. If 287 is correct, every interpolated identification in Shlyakhtenko's Theorem 1 collapses to L(Gamma) = L(F_2).
shlyakhtenko_check.verdict: The citation is real, correctly identified (ID, sole author, title, v1 date), and accurately summarised by 287 ('free complement to a commutator ... finite automorphisms and a limiting generation argument'). 287's claim that no result is used is consistent with the comparison: none of S_f, R_m, Q_q or the Baire Prop 1 appears in 287. The preprint is itself declared model-assisted (ChatGPT Pro 6.0). It contains close variants of 287's outer architecture: the one-step 'small automorphism improving approximation' step, the Nielsen-transvection conjugation, and limiting generation. It contains none of 287's inner mechanism: no small-cocycle lemma, no cocycle-driven flow in the final argument, no Arg(C). Net effect on grading: I31, I34 and the Nielsen correction drop to N2/N1. The eureka candidacy concentrates on the small-cocycle lemma I23 and its coupling I15.

family_D.label: D3 (provisional)
family_D.rests_on: C2 alone (I23), whose N3 meaning attaches to the cluster C2+C4. All other candidates are N0-N2.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if Test 4 arm B (cluster) exceeds the calibrated threshold, or if an expert identifies a known prescribed-value cocycle statement for groups with beta_1^(2) > 0.
family_D.not_transfer: The ingredients (Fox calculus, free CLT, free Khintchine, IPP logarithm, cyclomorphy) are transfer/N0. The candidate is their coupling, so the cross-field-transfer exclusion does not apply.
family_D.correctness_caveat: All grades are conditional on the proof being correct. The claim is unrefereed and extraordinary. Per lean.md, the comparator allInterpolatedIsomorphic has no sorry/axiom/native_decide, uses only the permitted axioms, and imports only Mathlib, but Lean was not run (compile status unverified). The Lean route differs from the paper: the n=2 step is proved directly via smallCocycleTwo, generation uses Baire, the small cocycle uses a radial averaged inverse, and the interpolation layer is re-proved. Non-integer L(F_r) is defined through Dykema's formula (trusted).
family_D.compression_note: The Lean analyst's step-3b estimate finds no PHP-style multiplicative blow-up for any novel item. They are single-use bottleneck lemmas with shallow definitions and additive inlining cost. Even if C2 passes Test 4, the 'confirmed eureka step' route (PLAN step 9) will rest on the downstream-speedup test, not on compression.

The 287 trace never mentions it. The precedent nonetheless anticipates 287's outer architecture (small automorphisms, Nielsen transvection, limiting generation) 13 days before the 287 preprint date. Flag as 'model-produced precedent (architecture), not builds-on'. For contamination control, exclude 2609.11074 and any post-2026-09-10 model.
